transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2029-06-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Mosaic Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Zara Malik (ML)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Mosaic is evaluating where to run embeddings + rerank pipeline. They currently use an in-house vector index for top-k recall and a CPU-based cross-encoder for rerank which is too slow for production. Main concerns: throughput at 10M+ vectors, embedding dimensionality tradeoffs (768 vs 1536), tail latency (p95 < 120ms target for query path), security (data residency, KMS), and cost. Discussed Redwood Hosted for quick start, Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private/VPC for compliance. Agreed to run throughput projections and follow up with pricing and a technical deep dive.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and pain points
- Embedding dims and candidate recall vs rerank accuracy
- Vector DB integration options and hot cache strategies
- Hosting tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- Quantization and batch sizing to meet p95 targets
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we said 45 but we have 58 min booked so we can go deep, I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, thanks, I'm Priya, I run Search at Mosaic. Quick context: we power product search and a knowledge assistant for our enterprise customers. Latency and cost are both blown out — our cross-encoder rerank is killing throughput.
[00:32] Ethan: Quick clarifying q, when you say cross-encoder, is that an on-prem CPU pipeline or GCP-based?
[00:39] Liam: It's mostly a CPU pool on GCP right now, some spot instances, but the p95 goes above a second during peak. We need something around 100 to 120 ms at p95 for the interactive assistant.
[00:51] Zara: We tried smaller cross-encoder models but accuracy dropped more than we'd like, so we do a bi-encoder recall then cross-encoder rerank for top 50.
[01:06] Sofia: Got it. So architecture today: embed -> vector index lookup -> bi-encoder top K -> cross-encoder rerank. Where are you storing vectors?
[01:12] Priya: We have a managed index service (not naming here, it's basically a homegrown Faiss layer) running on a few VMs. Sync is in-house.
[01:20] Ethan: Do you do sharding already across nodes?
[01:22] Liam: Yeah sharded by vertical, but it's manual. Rebalancing is a pain.
[01:26] Sofia: Okay. The parts folks usually want help with are: host vs dedicated sizing, embedding dims and econ, and rerank placement — do you want to push the reranker into Redwood or keep it in your infra?
[01:38] Priya: Ideally keep control of data flow but we want Redwood to handle the heavy lifting for generation and efficient rerank. So we were thinking hybrid: your hosted embedding + candidate generator, then our rerank? Or maybe Redwood run a small, optimized reranker as a second stage?
[01:53] Ethan: Both are doable. Typical pattern: do bi-encoder recall with Redwood-hosted or customer-hosted embedders -> vector DB top-k -> optional lightweight cross-encoder on Redwood Dedicated with quantized model to get rerank < 100ms. Or keep cross-encoder internal if you need KMS keys in-house.
[02:12] Zara: When you say quantized, you mean int8 or int4? We've seen int8 hurt our small model accuracy on some datasets.
[02:20] Ethan: Right, we generally recommend 8-bit quant for the rerank surrogate or 4-bit for the bigger LMs, but of course we'd run evals. Another option is to use a distilled cross-encoder that's smaller (like a few hundred million params) which often keeps ranking quality with much lower cost.
[02:34] Priya: Our constraints: 10M vectors initially, expected to grow to 40M in 12 months. Query mix: 65% product search (short queries), 30% assistant (longer queries with context), 5% analytics. SLO: p95 < 120 ms for product search flow; assistant can be 200 ms for first stage but total end-to-end should be < 500 ms.
[02:56] Sofia: Excellent, that gives us something to size on. Ethan, can you capture throughput numbers for 10M and 40M with 768 vs 1536 dims?
[03:03] Ethan: Yep, I'll run a projection — we'll include continuous batch sizing and prefix cache impact.
[03:09] Priya: Also security: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS for keys, and audit logging that shows model and prompt-level access. Are those supported for Hosted?
[03:22] Sofia: Hosted has SOC2, but for KMS separation and full cust-managed keys you generally look at Private (VPC) or Dedicated with KMS integration. Hosted offers envelope encryption at rest; for strict compliance we recommend Private. We'll share the security packet.
[03:36] Liam: VPC is interesting because we have data residency requirements for EU customers.
[03:41] Sofia: Private supports region-specific deployments and on-prem packages if needed. Dedicated can be put into a customer's VPC as well for network isolation.
[03:47] Zara: Operationally, how do you handle cache for frequent queries? We see a heavy tail but top 1k queries are hot.
[03:56] Ethan: We have automatic hot-prefix caching and can configure TTLs per-route. For top-k embeddings, often a small LRU cache for embedding outputs plus a hot-vector cache in-memory reduces duplicate compute. Combined with KV cache for autoregressive calls, it's very effective.
[04:11] Priya: Client-side question: if we put embeddings in our vector DB (self-hosted or managed), do we lose batching benefits from Redwood?
[04:20] Ethan: Good question. You can still batch embedding generation with Redwood API. The main thing is where you persist vectors: if you keep persistence in your DB, Redwood is just the generator. If you use Redwood Dedicated to host the index (we can recommend partners or deploy an index on the same cluster), we can co-locate to reduce network io. But batching for embed generation is independent—it's about how you send requests to Redwood.
[04:39] Priya: For rerank latency, is it better to do rerank in the same network region as index nodes?
[04:45] Ethan: Yes, colocating reduces tail latency. That's why Dedicated or Private deployments are common when you have strict latency SLOs.
[04:52] Sofia: Let's talk numbers a bit — rough cost vs perf tradeoffs. If you do 1536-d embeddings you'll have larger vector DB size and slower recall but typically better recall upstream reducing reranker load. 768-d is smaller and faster, but might increase false negatives requiring a larger top-K or heavier rerank.
[05:10] Zara: We're curious if using hybrid search (lexical + vector) will change the K we need.
[05:15] Ethan: Hybrid often reduces the need for very high K in dense-only recall. Combining with lightweight filter removes lots of negatives so your reranker does less work.
[05:22] Priya: Could you show an example pipeline recommendation?
[05:25] Ethan: Sure — Stage 1: Redwood-hosted embedder or customer-hosted -> persist to vector DB. Stage 2: Vector DB top 200 using approximate search -> Stage 3: Redwood Dedicated lightweight cross-encoder rerank top 50 (quantized) or customer internal rerank if they need cust-managed keys.
[05:41] Sofia: Note on routing: Redwood can route queries by policy — latency-first for EU, cost-first for dev, etc. That helps keep costs down while meeting SLOs.
[05:51] Liam: What about autoscaling on Dedicated? Our traffic is spiky with 3x weekly peaks.
[05:56] Ethan: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. You can set guaranteed baseline with burst on top. And for extremely spiky, we sometimes recommend a hybrid with Hosted fallback for overflow.
[06:08] Priya: That fallback pattern — is there a risk of different quality if fallback uses a smaller model?
[06:12] Sofia: Yes, we document expected differences. We can set automatic fallback to a lower-cost model with output-labeling so your app can degrade gracefully. Also A/B tests for behavior.
[06:23] Zara: For the reranker model, can Redwood host our in-house distilled model?
[06:28] Ethan: Yes, you can bring-your-own-model. We can onboard and vet performance. We also provide quantization and kernel selection for faster inference.
[06:36] Priya: Do you have benchmarks for 1536-d embeddings at 10M vectors on Dedicated?
[06:41] Ethan: We have internal benchmarks — I can't drop the whole sheet here but I'll run a tailored projection. Typically recall latency depends more on index type (HNSW vs IVF+PQ), and whether you're using compressed vectors (PQ). With PQ and a good HNSW config, 1536-d at 10M can hit sub-50ms per shard on GPU-accelerated retrieval, but that's a ballpark.
[06:57] Liam: You're mentioning GPU for retrieval — does Redwood operate GPU-backed vector search or is that something we self-manage?
[07:03] Ethan: We can run vector search on GPU in Dedicated clusters — depending on the index. Not all index types benefit from GPU, but with quantized kernels and GPU-optimized ANN library, it helps for very large dims and high QPS.
[07:14] Priya: Let's talk about a proof-of-concept. We want to test: 10M vectors, 1536-d embeddings, top 200 recall with hybrid filters, cross-encoder rerank top 50 with p95 under 120ms for product search. Can Redwood support a POC with those constraints?
[07:33] Sofia: Yes — typical POC is 4 weeks: ingest sample dataset, run benchmark scenarios, tuning batch sizes and quantization, then handover recommendations. We'll scope infra (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and cost.
[07:45] Zara: Data sync question: if we go with Redwood-managed embedding storage, how do we handle incremental updates?
[07:51] Ethan: Incremental ingest via streaming API or batch loads. We support delta updates and background reindexing. For low-latency freshness, small batches or streaming is best.
[08:02] Priya: Any constraints on embedding dimensionality for Hosted?
[08:06] Sofia: Hosted supports standard dims; the main constraint is cost and throughput. Larger dims mean larger payloads and higher tokenization cost if generating embeddings via LLM. We'll include network egress considerations in the cost sheet.
[08:18] Priya: A slightly awkward thing — we have encrypted PII in some docs. Will Redwood see plain text embeddings?
[08:24] Ethan: Embeddings are derived from plaintext, so if you can't send raw PII to Hosted, you'd need Private deployment or to do embedding generation on-prem and only send vectors to Redwood if you want storage with Redwood. We support bring-your-own-embeddings as well.
[08:40] Liam: For Dedicated, how does upgrade/rollout work? We can't have downtime.
[08:45] Sofia: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback. Dedicated clusters can be configured with zero-downtime rolling updates; we'll show runbooks.
[08:54] Priya: Regarding observability — token-level cost, model latency breakdown per endpoint?
[08:59] Ethan: Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards, token cost breakdown and per-request traces if you enable tracing. You can also stream logs to an external SIEM.
[09:10] Zara: For the rerank stage, is it better to run a distilled cross-encoder or run a two-pass rerank with a pointwise scorer?
[09:18] Ethan: Distilled cross-encoders or bi-encoder+light cross-encoder are both common. Two-pass can be faster but risks missing fine reordering. We'll run evals against your ground truth.
[09:28] Priya: Ok can we talk about the cost model for Dedicated — how predictable is it?
[09:33] Sofia: Dedicated is commit-based with a baseline monthly cost for reserved capacity. You can add burst on-demand. For predictable throughput we recommend sizing to your 95th percentile peaks. We'll show scenarios in the pricing doc.
[09:45] Liam: If we need VPC connectivity for Dedicated, is that in scope?
[09:49] Ethan: Yes, Dedicated can be deployed into your VPC and we manage the nodes with VPN or VPC peering. Private is for even stricter requirements like air-gapped or on-prem.
[09:59] Priya: How do you handle data deletion/audit for GDPR?
[10:04] Sofia: We provide deletion APIs and audit logs. For Hosted we keep retention policies, but for strict regulatory needs we recommend Private where you control retention.
[10:14] Zara: Anything we should watch for in vector DB choice? We're considering a managed service vs self-hosted Faiss.
[10:21] Ethan: Think about scaling primitives: shard rebalancing, snapshot/restore, and support for PQ/compression. Managed services often provide easier ops but sometimes less flexibility for custom kernels.
[10:34] Priya: Are there rate limits on embeddings per minute for Hosted trials?
[10:38] Sofia: Trials have soft rate limits but we can flex for pilots. For production we size Dedicated.
[10:44] Liam: For the POC, timeline and data needed?
[10:47] Sofia: Ideally sample dataset (10-50k docs representing the 10M distribution), query logs, and target SLOs. We'll ingest a sample and run bench.
[10:58] Priya: We'll share sample logs and a shortlist of evaluation prompts.
[11:02] Zara: One last thought: does Redwood support model explainability or tokens attribution for rerank decisions?
[11:09] Ethan: We have tracing and token-level scoring; for deep explainability we can surface attention-like scores or gradients depending on model. It's part of the eval phase.
[11:18] Sofia: Great, let's talk next steps — I'll send a scope doc and a proposed POC plan. Ethan will run the sizing and benchmarks and we'll get security docs over to you.
[11:27] Priya: Sounds good. Can we schedule the deep dive on 6/12 afternoon?
[11:30] Sofia: I'll propose a slot; Ethan, are you available?
[11:33] Ethan: Yes.
[11:34] Priya: Also, can you include cost per 1M queries for hosted vs dedicated rough numbers?
[11:38] Sofia: We'll include a cost-per-query estimate and a 12-month TCO comparison.
[11:42] Liam: For the action items, Priya will send sample logs.
[11:46] Priya: Yep, I'll get those by Friday.
[11:49] Sofia: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the sheet and security packet.
[11:53] Priya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript
